purpose: Compare a frozen 2024 pretrained text encoder with the tuned TF-IDF SVM, and measure the effect of additional training requirements on fixed held-out projects.
status: Exploratory development after original and SecReq outcomes were inspected. PROMISE+ eligibility and project partition fixed before any classifier prediction on PROMISE+.
data_preparation: Use the copied audit's project exclusions and seed-42 half-project partition. Additionally remove auxiliary training statements flagged by the same near-match screen against either fixed test corpus. Do not modify labels or inspect model performance to alter membership.
binary_mapping: Published F maps to FR; all eleven named NFR quality classes map to NFR. Retain source labels in output. This is a binary reduction, not native FR/NFR string labels.

encoder.fitting: Frozen; no encoder training or adaptation on any requirement data
encoder.pooling: First CLS token, L2 normalised, no retrieval query prefix

selection: Highest mean macro F1 on exactly the same five original-training folds. No external result, external embedding or auxiliary label is used to select the semantic head. First listed candidate wins an exact tie.
comparisons: Original-trained tuned TF-IDF unigram+bigram balanced SVM from experiment 03
Original-trained frozen-encoder SVM selected using original training folds
Fixed experiment-03 word settings refitted on original training plus auxiliary projects
Selected semantic-head settings refitted on original training plus auxiliary projects
augmentation_selection: No additional search or resampling. Reuse the selected settings; report both original-only and augmented conditions regardless of outcome. An augmented model has seen other PROMISE+ projects and cannot be described as source-unseen on PROMISE+.
evaluation: All five models on the same original holdout, unchanged SecReq and the 802-record PROMISE+ test. Accuracy, macro precision/recall/F1, per-class metrics, confusion matrices, per-project results and both constant-label baselines. No model is selected or deployed using test scores.
stopping_rule: Complete the recorded comparisons and independent verification once. Do not alter data, labels, random seed or search in response to missing 80-90%.
limitations: Existing original and SecReq test outcomes were already known; follow-up evidence is exploratory.
Whole-project exclusions reduce observed overlap but original source IDs are absent; unseen underlying projects or semantic overlap cannot be fully proved.
Source labels include arguable mixed functional/security/business-rule cases. No independent gold-label reannotation is claimed.
PROMISE+ includes older requirements; 2024 is the release date. Some text contains source encoding artefacts or context dependence, retained unchanged.
The additional-training condition measures transfer to held-out project IDs within a source already represented in training, not unseen-source performance.
Higher scores on PROMISE+ do not erase the SecReq result or establish performance on every new project.
No guaranteed 80-90% score and no inferred time savings or human-accuracy improvement.
app_deployment: No automatic replacement of the application's existing model. Save all candidate heads and fitted word pipelines separately.
